notes: Independent ranking-evidence pass covers all 15 records from discovery (10) and diamond expansion (5); the fee audit was read. Only difficulty and metrics are replaced. Six provisional high judgments, one moderate judgment and eight unknown bands are retained. These are agent judgments within the named specialties, not measured acceptance odds, a total ordering across psychology, or a comparison across disciplines.

Five Sage acceptance rates were directly read from official dashboards: Applied Psychological Measurement 13.0%, Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin 18.4%, Group Processes & Intergroup Relations 13.4%, Theory & Psychology 10.0%, and European Journal of Personality 17.4%. The live Sage definition (https://www.sagepub.com/journals/understanding-journal-metrics) explicitly defines the period as the previous calendar year and the population as all final accept/reject decisions, across all article types. The dashboards do not print the year or denominator counts. Therefore year fields preserve the relative period; 2025 is identified only as an inference from the 2026 check date. Rates cannot be treated as externally reviewed-only, submission-cohort rates, future acceptance chances or causal effects of choosing a journal.

Sage dashboards also report median handling times, but the inspected current guide does not give an unambiguous reporting period for those speed measures; they are omitted from metrics. Culture & Psychology and Feminism & Psychology overview/metric retrievals were incomplete or timed out, so no numerical metrics are invented. The Group Processes instructions were successfully read at the uppercase GPI URL after repeated lowercase-URL timeouts. Ordinary urllib access to Sage returned HTTP 403; official browser-accessible pages supplied the evidence used here.

Retained eight explicitly year-labeled citation metrics across Psychological Research, Memory & Cognition, Methodology and Social Psychological Bulletin, plus two explicitly 2024 publication-volume counts for Judgment and Decision Making. JIF and five-year definitions were checked in the official Sage guide; CiteScore's four-year numerator/denominator definition was independently checked in the official Elsevier Scopus support page (https://www.elsevier.support/scopus/answer/what-is-citescore). Citation values are contextual information and are not used to assign difficulty bands.

Judgment and Decision Making's official metric page lists a 2-year Impact Factor of 2.5, a 5-year Impact Factor of 2.8, CiteScore 3.6 and other citation figures without an explicit citation year in the inspected rendering (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/judgment-and-decision-making/information/about-this-journal/journal-metrics). Those ambiguous-period figures are not entered as dated metrics. Its publication-count table explicitly states 2024 and reports 35 research-type articles and 35 OA articles; the counting guide is volume-based. Neither count demonstrates a current free route or a submission acceptance rate.

Meta-Psychology's moderate judgment is based on its explicit no-quota, no-target-rejection-rate and no-novelty-criterion policy, while preserving high scientific quality, distinct contribution, desk review, expert open review and statistical reproduction requirements (https://open.lnu.se/index.php/metapsychology/about). No rate was calculated from its public OSF submission history. Its About page and newer submission instructions differ on preregistration wording; the newer instructions require it for data-collecting or confirmatory work (https://open.lnu.se/index.php/metapsychology/about/submissions). A moderate band does not remove those manuscript-specific conditions.

Preserved the independently audited fee and availability restrictions. PsychOpen GOLD officially announces discontinuation by 31 December 2027 and transition support (https://psychopen.eu/); current metrics do not establish successor terms or future availability. The fee audit's paused Journal of Numerical Cognition, Europe's Journal of Psychology, and Journal of Social and Political Psychology leads are not added or treated as reopened by this pass. Psychological Thought's current university-hosted evidence is distinct from the PsychOpen transition.

Preserved Social Psychological Bulletin's prohibition of AI-written original text even when disclosed (https://spb.psychopen.eu/index.php/spb/author-policies), and Theory & Psychology's requirement for disclosure plus explicit editorial permission for AI-generated text or visuals (https://journals.sagepub.com/author-instructions/tap). Ranking and free-route status do not authorize a manuscript workflow.

Missing metrics remain empty arrays, with no null-valued metric placeholders. The pass inspected the cited official pages and linked editorial criteria; it did not contact editors, log in, submit manuscripts, establish scientific suitability for a particular study or perform human scientific review. No fees or canonical records were edited.
